hints: Write Newton's second law for the heavier descending particle ($0.8\text{ kg}$): $0.8g - T = 0.8a$.
Write Newton's second law for the lighter ascending particle ($0.2\text{ kg}$): $T - 0.2g = 0.2a$.
Add the two equations to eliminate $T$ and find $a$, then substitute $a$ back to find $T$.
walkthrough:
Apply Newton's second law vertically downwards to the $0.8\text{ kg}$ particle with $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$0.8g - T = 0.8a$$
$$8 - T = 0.8a \quad \text{--- (Equation 1)}$$

Apply Newton's second law vertically upwards to the $0.2\text{ kg}$ particle:
$$T - 0.2g = 0.2a$$
$$T - 2 = 0.2a \quad \text{--- (Equation 2)}$$

Add Equation 1 and Equation 2 to eliminate $T$:
$$(8 - T) + (T - 2) = 0.8a + 0.2a$$
$$6 = 1.0a \implies a = 6\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Substitute $a = 6\text{ m s}^{-2}$ into Equation 2 to find tension $T$:
$$T - 2 = 0.2(6) = 1.2$$
$$T = 2 + 1.2 = 3.2\text{ N}$$

ai_rubric.Solving Connected-Particle Systems: Sets up $0.8g - T = 0.8a$ and $T - 0.2g = 0.2a$, solves to show $a = 6\text{ m s}^{-2}$ and finds $T = 3.2\text{ N}$.

teacher_walkthrough: Consider the system of two particles connected by a light inextensible string over a fixed smooth pulley.

Isolate the heavier particle of mass $m_1 = 0.8\text{ kg}$, which accelerates downwards:
$$m_1 g - T = m_1 a$$
Substitute $m_1 = 0.8\text{ kg}$ and $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$0.8(10) - T = 0.8a$$
$$8 - T = 0.8a \quad \text{(Equation 1)}$$

Isolate the lighter particle of mass $m_2 = 0.2\text{ kg}$, which accelerates upwards with the same acceleration $a$:
$$T - m_2 g = m_2 a$$
Substitute $m_2 = 0.2\text{ kg}$ and $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$T - 0.2(10) = 0.2a$$
$$T - 2 = 0.2a \quad \text{(Equation 2)}$$

Add Equation 1 and Equation 2 to eliminate the internal tension $T$:
$$(8 - T) + (T - 2) = 0.8a + 0.2a$$
$$6 = 1.0a$$
$$a = 6\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Substitute $a = 6\text{ m s}^{-2}$ into Equation 2 to find the tension $T$:
$$T - 2 = 0.2(6)$$
$$T - 2 = 1.2$$
$$T = 2 + 1.2 = 3.2\text{ N}$$

hints: Find the speed $v$ of the particles when the $0.8\text{ kg}$ particle hits the floor after descending $0.5\text{ m}$ with $a = 6\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
At this instant, the $0.2\text{ kg}$ particle has risen $0.5\text{ m}$ to a height of $1.0\text{ m}$ above the floor.
After the string goes slack, the $0.2\text{ kg}$ particle moves freely under gravity ($a = -10\text{ m s}^{-2}$). Use $0 = v^2 - 2gs$ to find the additional height.
Add the initial height ($0.5\text{ m}$), the distance moved during acceleration ($0.5\text{ m}$), and the extra free-flight height.
walkthrough:
Calculate the speed $v$ of the particles at the instant the $0.8\text{ kg}$ particle reaches the floor ($s = 0.5\text{ m}$, $a = 6\text{ m s}^{-2}$):
$$v^2 = u^2 + 2as = 0 + 2(6)(0.5) = 6$$
$$v = \sqrt{6}\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
At this point, the $0.2\text{ kg}$ particle is at height $h_1 = 0.5 + 0.5 = 1.0\text{ m}$ above the floor.

The string becomes slack and the $0.2\text{ kg}$ particle ascends freely under gravity ($a = -g = -10\text{ m s}^{-2}$) until $v = 0$:
$$0 = v^2 - 2gs_{\text{extra}}$$
$$0 = 6 - 2(10)s_{\text{extra}}$$
$$20s_{\text{extra}} = 6 \implies s_{\text{extra}} = \frac{6}{20} = 0.3\text{ m}$$

Compute the greatest height of the $0.2\text{ kg}$ particle above the floor:
$$h_{\text{max}} = 0.5 + 0.5 + 0.3 = 1.3\text{ m}$$

ai_rubric.Modelling Vertical Motion: Finds $v^2 = 6$, calculates free-flight height $s = 6/20 = 0.3\text{ m}$, and obtains greatest height $0.5 + 0.5 + 0.3 = 1.3\text{ m}$.

teacher_walkthrough:
First phase (Connected motion): The $0.8\text{ kg}$ particle falls through $s = 0.5\text{ m}$ from rest with acceleration $a = 6\text{ m s}^{-2}$. Use the constant-acceleration formula:
$$v^2 = u^2 + 2as$$
$$v^2 = 0 + 2(6)(0.5) = 6$$
$$v = \sqrt{6}\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

During this phase, the $0.2\text{ kg}$ particle rises by the exact same distance $0.5\text{ m}$. Since it started $0.5\text{ m}$ above the floor, its height at the moment the string goes slack is:
$$h_1 = 0.5 + 0.5 = 1.0\text{ m}$$

Second phase (Free vertical flight): The string is now slack, so the $0.2\text{ kg}$ particle projects upwards under gravity alone with initial upward velocity $u = \sqrt{6}\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and acceleration $a = -g = -10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

At the maximum height of its flight, its velocity becomes zero ($v = 0$):
$$v^2 = u^2 + 2as$$
$$0 = (\sqrt{6})^2 + 2(-10)s_{\text{extra}}$$
$$0 = 6 - 20s_{\text{extra}}$$
$$20s_{\text{extra}} = 6$$
$$s_{\text{extra}} = \frac{6}{20} = 0.3\text{ m}$$

Calculate the greatest height above the floor by adding all three heights:
$$H = h_{\text{initial}} + s_{\text{connected}} + s_{\text{extra}} = 0.5 + 0.5 + 0.3 = 1.3\text{ m}$$
